title: Introduce cost-runner sandbox and progressive quant annealer
author: Ava Martinez
description: Context: Customers running at scale need safe, measurable ways to explore cost/latency tradeoffs. This PR adds a sandboxed "cost-runner" that replays live or synthetic traffic against candidate batching, caching and quantization configurations and a progressive quant annealer that can safely propose staged quant changes per-model (layer-aware) with unit-economics breakpoints and rollback policies. Motivation: previous manual experiments required adhoc scripts and produced noisy telemetry; teams asked for a reproducible, CI-friendly path to evaluate cost-first defaults. What this PR delivers: 1) cost-runner CLI (crun) - run deterministic simulation using captured traces or synthetic generators, supports shadowing to live endpoints, dry-run mode, and outputting summary reports (token counts, per-token cost, latency p95/99, inferred unit-econ delta) 2) progressive-quant annealer - a staged quant application engine (float32 -> int8/4 -> mixed-int) that applies layer groups and monitors quality thresholds with automatic rollback triggers based on evals and unit-econ thresholds 3) sandbox telemetry - new cost_signals metric family and a compact schema for per-sample cost attribution, batch-shape histograms, and quant-impact deltas 4) safety/rollout primitives - a new safety_gate policy that wires into existing rollouts and can block a quant-stage if unit-econ regressions exceed configured budgets 5) docs, examples and integration tests. Checklist: - [x] crun CLI and core simulator - [x] annealer algorithms and simple heuristic scheduler - [x] telemetry schema + exporters - [x] safety gate + rollout integration - [x] docs and example workload - [x] integration tests and smoke CI. How to use: run `crun simulate --trace sample.json --policy progressive-quant --out report.json` to produce a reproducible report; use `crun apply --dry-run` to preview rollout plan. Related: Linear ENG-3241 (cost-runner design), ENG-3310 (progressive quant requirements). Risks & mitigations: quant staging can alter output quality; annealer runs include mandatory eval checkpoints and an opt-in fail-open flag for exploratory customers. Performance impact: negligible at runtime for non-sandboxed paths; when the rollout is live the safety gate adds a ~2ms decision check. Backwards compatibility: none of the changes alter existing runtime paths unless customers opt into the annealer or install the crun flow. Link to design doc: https://linear.app/ENG-3241/design/cost-runner-sandbox (internal).
